# A certified bracket for the Erdos-Herzog-Piranian infimum

*Generated by tools/build-lemniscate-writeup.js from certs/erdos1038-inf.json
at git 0ce3ff7. Every constant below is interpolated from that record.*

## Abstract

For a nonconstant monic polynomial f with all roots in [-1,1], Erdos, Herzog
and Piranian (1958) asked for the extremes of the measure of the set where f
has modulus below 1. Writing mu for the root measure and U_mu(x) for the
logarithmic
potential, the integral of log(1/|x-t|) against mu, the quantity is the measure
of the set where U_mu < 0. We prove, in outward-rounded interval arithmetic
with a machine-checkable certificate,

    1.828 <= inf over mu of |{U_mu < 0}| <= 1.8344304971959906.

The lower bound uses no tail estimate, assumes no minimizer, and argues by no
contradiction: it is a direct forcing argument whose only analytic input beyond
interval arithmetic is the symmetry of the mutual energy, that the integral of
U_nu against mu equals the integral of U_mu against nu. We further answer
affirmatively, for every eps in (0, 0.1], the model problem posed as Problem
4.1 in Tao's notes on this problem, and we certify three dual measures posted
by the community which had previously been validated by sampling only.

Three AI-assisted proofs claiming the exact value D = 1.83443047576266171109... are outstanding
at the time of writing (Section 5). THIS PAPER ASSUMES NONE OF THEM and
adjudicates none of them; the bracket above is unconditional.

## 1. Setting

Every nonconstant monic f of degree d with roots in [-1,1] corresponds to the
root measure mu, the average of point masses at the roots, and f(x) has modulus
below 1 exactly where U_mu(x) > 0 after the standard normalization; passing to
general
probability measures on [-1,1] is the usual closure. The two extremes are
independent problems. The supremum is the subject of a separate certified
program of ours and is not treated here.

## 2. The upper bound

THEOREM 1. For the probability measure mu = A d_{-1} + f(y) dy on [a,1], where
d_{-1} is the unit mass at -1, with the exact rational parameters

    a = 0.804462,   A = 0.8245218,
    f(y) = [1 - A sqrt(2(1+a))/(1+y)] / (pi sqrt((y-a)(1-y))),

the set where U_mu < 0 is the interval (x_L, x_R) with the point -1 removed,

    x_L in [-1.8081074413361424, -1.808107441336006],
    x_R in [0.02632305585964334, 0.026323055859847976],

so the infimum is at most 1.8344304971959906.

The potential off the support is c + g(x) - A g_Omega(x,-1) in the Joukowski
coordinate, with c the constant on-support level and g the Green's functions of
the complement; the certificate verifies c >= 0 (certified c in
[9.315e-8, 9.315e-8]), the
nonnegativity of the density, and the two root enclosures. The set structure
follows from three one-line lemmas: the sign of U' left of -1, concavity on
(-1,a), and positivity right of 1. Classical inputs: the arcsine potential
identity and the balayage of a point mass onto an interval (Saff-Totik), each
bridged numerically in the lab.

## 3. The lower bound

THEOREM 2. The infimum is at least 1.828.

Under the standard reduction — mu normalized with support inside {-1} union
[0,1], and the interval (-sqrt2, 0) contained in E, the set where U_mu > 0 —
let a_0 be the infimum of the component of E containing (-sqrt2, 0). Then
U_mu(a_0) <= 0 by lower semicontinuity and a_0 lies in [-2, -sqrt2].

THE SELECTOR. If nu is a finite atomic measure, a unit mass at a_0 plus
nonnegative weights w_i at points p_i, and U_nu > 0 on the support of mu, then
the symmetry of the mutual energy forces at least one p_i to lie in E.

THE COMB. If a_0 <= -cap the component already has length at least cap.
Otherwise, with R = cap - |a_0|, the certificate exhibits for every b in [0,R]
a measure nu_b — the mass at a_0, a heavy atom at b, and descending teeth at
s_j - b — with U_{nu_b} > 0 on {-1} union [0,1], hence on the support of mu.
The atoms travel at unit speed along pairwise disjoint images, all disjoint
from (a_0, 0), so the selector gives |E| >= |a_0| + R = cap.

WHAT IS CERTIFIED. The parameter a_0 is tiled by 86 boxes over the
full range [-cap, -sqrt2]; each carries one comb, and 1,350 b-boxes in
total, each with one frozen weight vector obtained from a floating-point linear
program and then VERIFIED by intervals, never trusted. Two monotonicity facts
collapse the two-parameter problem to thin one-dimensional convex problems:
U_nu(x) increases in a_0 for x > a_0, and in the shifted coordinate y = x + b
the teeth do not move while the remainder increases in b. Convex pole sums are
bounded below by interval tangent lines between consecutive poles and bisected
to positivity. Worst certified margin over all boxes:
4.116e-7; runtime 265 seconds.

An independent checker (verify-forcing.js, sharing no code with the certifier)
re-derives the tiling and weight structure from the certificate file and
searches for counterexamples in floating point; it reports no violation.

REMARK (the ceiling of the method). The same forcing at the conjectured optimum
can move the free atom only as far as x_R, about 0.0263, so this route cannot
exceed the Theorem 1 value — the method is exact in principle. The comb family
in particular is exhausted near 1.828: its certified margin has thinned to
4.12e-7 and finer boxes cannot buy the next
thousandth. Passing it requires demanding positivity only on the minimizer's
own support, which is a different construction rather than a longer run.

## 4. Tao's Problem 4.1, and a mechanism

THEOREM 3. For every eps in (0, 0.1] the explicit measure lambda^(eps) is
positive with U_lambda >= 0 on all of [-1,1]; the two-interval scenario is
therefore excluded for the whole range.

The certificate covers [1e-12, 0.1] with 624,275 interval
chunks, each carrying its own rational parameter, and a separate sliver lemma
closes (0, 1e-12] by the substitution t = zeta_1 - 1, under which the
eps -> 0 singular pole cancels algebraically rather than numerically.

THE DELTA-MECHANISM. As eps tends to 0 the margin at x = -1 tends to a constant
delta determined by the level defect of the primal constants. With rounded
constants delta may have either sign, and if it is negative the family PROVABLY
FAILS for eps below roughly |delta|/0.21. This was not anticipated: the
certifier returned a decisively negative window and the mechanism was
identified afterwards to explain it. Constructions built from midpoint decimals
will meet this wall; all constructions posted on the problem's forum sit far
above it. Our test suite keeps the failure as a control — putting the defect on
the wrong side must make the certificate refuse.

THEOREM 4 (community measures). The three dual measures posted on the forum,
previously validated by sampling, are positive with U_lambda >= 0 on [-1,1];
certified off-atom minima
1.243e-5, 2.653e-6, 3.959e-6.
Positivity is established by adaptive tangent envelopes on each gap between
support points — no quadrature and no grid, which is what sampling could not
supply.

## 5. Relation to the outstanding claims

At the time of writing the problem's forum lists three claimed full proofs, all
AI-assisted, each reporting the same value D = 1.83443047576266171109...: Darvas, Peng and
Runzhou Tao (2026-07-15, GPT-5.5 Pro in a prover-verifier framework); Shouqiao
Wang (GPT-5.6 Sol); and Cristian Budala (2026-08-24, GPT-5.6 Sol). The forum
states that appearing there "is no guarantee of proof correctness, and does not
mean that anyone associated with this site has examined any part of the proof."

We have separately re-verified the COMPUTATIONAL APPENDIX of the Darvas-Peng-Tao
manuscript — existence and local uniqueness of the extremal triple by an
interval Krawczyk operator, and all thirty printed decimals of D — and we did
NOT audit its analytic core. Nothing in the present paper depends on any of the
three. Our bracket contains D, which is corroboration and not confirmation.

**[OPERATOR] decision.** Whether to submit this while three claimed solutions
are outstanding, and if so how to frame the contribution — the unconditional
bracket, the tail-free forcing method, and Problem 4.1 — is a judgment call.

## 6. Reproduction

    node tools/run-lemniscate.js
    node instruments/lemniscate/forcing.js 1.828 certs/erdos1038-forcing-1.828.json
    node instruments/lemniscate/battery.js

The first recomputes Theorems 1, 3 and 4 and re-verifies the forcing record;
the second rebuilds that record from scratch; the third runs the checks and the
red controls, every one of which must fire. The certifier is
instruments/interval — outward-rounded interval arithmetic with BigInt rational
falsifiers — the same one behind this repository's other certified theorems.
Records: certs/erdos1038-inf.json and certs/erdos1038-forcing-1.828.json.
